title: SIEM Adapters — Customer Requirements Workbench
content:
Purpose:
This workbench is a single-page, operational requirements and connector-spec reference for SIEM exports (Splunk, Datadog, Azure Sentinel) focused on: customer onboarding requirements, RBAC v2 considerations for export access, audit-log schema mapping to SIEM fields, and evidence-automation integration patterns.

Audience:
- Solutions engineers onboarding customers for SIEM exports
- Connector engineers implementing and testing adapters
- Compliance owners validating evidence automation contracts

Executive summary:
Customers ask for predictable, auditable exports of telemetry (audit logs, request traces, security events). This doc: (1) captures minimum ingestion requirements for three target SIEMs, (2) defines the canonical audit_log schema and mapping rules, (3) lists RBAC v2 constraints and recommended service-account scopes, and (4) prescribes evidence-automation anchors used by customer SOC playbooks.

1) Minimum customer requirements checklist (pre-onboarding)
- Identify target SIEM provider and intake mechanism: Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs HTTP Intake, Azure Monitor Data Collector (Log Analytics).
- Network: IPs/subnets for egress allowed, or VPC/peering details for private connectors.
- Ingestion auth: token secret, certs, or Azure Managed Identity details.
- Retention & legal holds: customer retention window and any legal-hold policy.
- PII/data-scope declaration: what fields must be redacted before export.
- Throughput estimate: average events/sec and peak bursts.
- Time sync requirements: customer requires event timestamps in UTC ISO8601.
- Test dataset: sample 1000 events representative of production for validation.

2) Canonical audit_log event schema (single-line description for mapping)
- log_id: unique id for event (uuid)
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC
- principal: { id, type, org_id } -> stringified in SIEM as principal_id, principal_type, org
- action: short action key (e.g., token.create, model.invoke)
- resource: resource identifier (model: model_id, route: route_id)
- outcome: success | failure | throttled
- client_ip: client IP address (if present)
- user_agent: client UA string
- request_id: tracing request id
- latency_ms: numeric latency in milliseconds
- token_cost: token/usage billing amount (for cost-related alerts)
- metadata: free-form key=value pairs (flatten before export)

Mapping rules (general):
- Flatten nested 'principal' and 'resource' objects into top-level SIEM fields with a consistent prefix (e.g., principal_id, resource_type).
- Drop null/empty fields.
- Convert booleans to strings where target SIEM has schema constraints.
- Timestamp must be parsed by the SIEM as event timestamp; include both event_timestamp and ingest_timestamp if possible.

3) Target SIEM adapter specifics
A. Splunk (HTTP Event Collector - HEC)
- Auth: HEC token header 'Authorization: Splunk <token>'.
- Endpoint: https://input-<realm>.splunkcloud.com:8088/services/collector/event
- Preferred payload: JSON per-line event or event batching with 'event' wrapper.
- Recommended fields: time (seconds since epoch float), host (redwood-instance or customer-id), index (customer-index), sourcetype: redwood:audit_log.v1
- Example single event (payload):
  {
    "event": {
      "log_id": "b7f...",
      "timestamp": "2026-03-09T13:12:02Z",
      "principal_id": "user_123",
      "action": "model.invoke",
      "outcome": "success",
      "latency_ms": 42
    },
    "sourcetype": "redwood:audit_log:v1"
  }
- Throughput: HEC batch maximum recommended 2000 events/batch or ~1MB per request; tune for network and customer SLA.
- Splunk-specific considerations: ensure proper sourcetype and index mapping; provide ingestion props/transforms if customer requires field aliasing.

B. Datadog (Logs HTTP Intake)
- Auth: API key in header 'DD-API-KEY: <key>' or use proxy with API key rotation.
- Endpoint: https://http-intake.logs.datadoghq.com/api/v2/logs
- Preferred payload: JSON array of log objects; each object may include ddsource, ddtags, hostname, service.
- Required mapping: set ddsource: redwood.audit, service: <customer-service>, host: <customer-host>
- Example single event (payload):
  {
    "message": "{\"log_id\":\"...\", \"action\":\"model.invoke\"}",
    "ddsource": "redwood.audit",
    "ddtags": "env:prod,customer:acme",
    "service": "redwood-inference",
    "hostname": "redwood-host"
  }
- Datadog recommends max 5MB per request; batch events up to 1000. Include source and service to enable log-based metrics.

C. Azure Sentinel / Log Analytics (Data Collector API)
- Auth: Shared key or Azure Managed Identity through MSI (preferred for private deployments).
- Endpoint: https://<workspaceId>.ods.opinsights.azure.com/api/logs?api-version=2016-04-01
- Preferred payload: JSON array of flattened objects. Each event maps to a custom record type 'Redwood_Audit_CL' (Custom Log).
- Must include: TimeGenerated (ISO8601), Computer (host/customer), and _ResourceId if applicable.
- Example event body (single entry):
  {
    "log_id": "...",
    "TimeGenerated": "2026-03-09T13:12:02Z",
    "principal_id": "user_123",
    "action": "model.invoke",
    "outcome": "success"
  }
- Azure requires a content-length, x-ms-date, and signature header computed with workspace key.

4) RBAC v2 considerations for exports
- Principle of least privilege: create a dedicated service role for SIEM exports with minimal abilities: read-audit-logs, read-request-traces. Do not grant write-to-billing or admin scopes.
- Short-lived tokens for connectors: prefer rotating tokens (30-day max) and recommend using customer-managed secrets (KMS/HSM) for private deployment connectors.
- Audit trail: every connector action (start/stop/config-change) should produce an audit log entry that includes operator_id, config_delta, and request_id.
- Multi-tenant separation: for Hosted API, enforce tenant scoping via org_id filtering and token-scoped indexes.

5) Evidence automation integration patterns
- Anchor events: for any compliance/evidence artifact generated (e.g., model-explain log, evaluation snapshot), include a stable evidence_id and link_url. The SIEM event should include evidence_id so SOC playbooks can fetch artifacts.
- Evidence storage: artifacts stored in customer-owned S3/GCS with signed short-lived URLs (expiration 7–30 days) or in Redwood-managed evidence store depending on contract.
- Automation hooks: include an 'evidence' object in events with fields: evidence_id, artifact_type, artifact_url, retention_policy. Flatten artifact_url for SIEMs that do not support nested fields.
- Sample evidence-augmented event JSON (flattened):
  {
    "log_id": "...",
    "timestamp": "2026-03-09T13:12:02Z",
    "action": "model.release",
    "evidence_id": "ev_2026_00421",
    "evidence_url": "https://s3.amazonaws.com/acme-evidence/ev_2026_00421.tar.gz",
    "evidence_type": "release-bundle",
    "outcome": "success"
  }

6) Data governance — redaction, PII, and tokenization
- Redaction rules: apply server-side redaction rules prior to export. Configurable regex masks for email, credit-card-like numbers, SSNs. Redaction must be documented per customer.
- Tokenization: when required, replace PII values with reversible tokens stored in a secure vault; include token_reference field in exported events to support rehydration under legal conditions.
- Field allowlist/denylist: customers must confirm which metadata fields are allowed to leave Redwood. Default denylist includes full prompt text for customer with sensitive data unless explicitly approved.

7) Throughput, batching, and cost guidance
- Suggested defaults: batch size 500 events or 256KB per request; tune upward for low-latency tolerant customers.
- Backpressure: if SIEM returns 429, connector should implement exponential backoff with jitter and buffer events to S3/GCS for replays.
- Replay window: keep 7 days of replayable batches for safety (configurable). Document replay process for customer SOC.

8) Testing, validation, and acceptance criteria
- Unit validation: schema conformance tests for canonical audit_log -> adapter payload.
- Integration testing: send 1k events to customer test endpoint, validate timestamps, field mapping, and event counts in SIEM.
- Evidence validation: verify evidence_url resolution and permissions by fetching sample artifact from SOC-run script.
- Acceptance criteria: 99% of test events parsed into expected index/sourcetype within 60s of ingest, zero PII leaks in a 1000-event sample.

9) Operational runbook (high level)
- Alerting: connectors emit health pings to Monitoring (redwood-monitoring) and raise PagerDuty when ingestion error rate >1% for 10m.
- Troubleshooting steps: check token validity, network connectivity, payload schema, rate-limit headers from SIEM.
- Replay flows: documented CLI to re-enqueue batches from replay storage (S3/GCS) with dry-run and commit flags.

10) Security controls and compliance notes
- Transport: TLS1.2+ mandatory; mTLS supported for private connectors.
- Secrets: store secrets in customer KMS where available; rotate on breach or annually.
- Auditability: record connector configuration snapshots and who changed them.
- Certifications: document any SOC2/ISO artefacts required for customer review; provide redacted evidence when requested.

Appendix A — sample full flattened event (canonical)
{
  "log_id": "b7f3d2c6-6a9b-4c5b-9c9f-11d2a8f0ef00",
  "timestamp": "2026-03-09T13:12:02Z",
  "ingest_timestamp": "2026-03-09T13:12:03Z",
  "principal_id": "user_123",
  "principal_type": "user",
  "org_id": "org_45",
  "action": "model.invoke",
  "resource_type": "model",
  "resource_id": "gptx-4.5-mini",
  "request_id": "req_7890",
  "outcome": "success",
  "client_ip": "203.0.113.42",
  "user_agent": "redwood-sdk/1.12.0",
  "latency_ms": "42",
  "token_cost": "0.0034",
  "evidence_id": "ev_2026_00421",
  "evidence_url": "https://s3.amazonaws.com/acme-evidence/ev_2026_00421.tar.gz"
}

Appendix B — quick connector config snippets
- Splunk HEC curl (single event):
curl -k \
  -H 'Authorization: Splunk ${HEC_TOKEN}' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"event": <EVENT_JSON>}' \
  https://input-aws-us-east-1.splunkcloud.com:8088/services/collector/event

- Datadog (batch upload):
curl -X POST https://http-intake.logs.datadoghq.com/api/v2/logs \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'DD-API-KEY: ${DD_API_KEY}' \
  -d '[<EVENT_JSON_1>, <EVENT_JSON_2>]'

Appendix C — common gotchas
- Nested objects lost: some SIEMs flatten or truncate nested objects — always pre-flatten critical keys.
- Timestamp drift: ensure client and connector clocks use NTP; include ingest_timestamp to aid debugging.
- Large artifacts: do not embed large binary artifacts in events; always use artifact URLs.

Owner notes & next steps:
- SEs: use this workbench to populate the onboarding questionnaire for each customer.
- Connector engineers: implement the schema transformation layer and include schema validation unit-tests.
- Compliance: review redaction rules and sign-off on default denylist before enabling exports for customers with sensitive workloads.
